🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-07 23:00 → 2026-10-08 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **evaluate() verdict-boundary enforcement landed on PR #59** — commit a05099e tightens the gate so only NO_FINDING and CONTRADICTED verdicts without a grade pass through, and c7 makes NOT_VALID reachable, closing the structural gap. [tg:tawg:5349]

> **PR #59 structural invariant confirmed at commit a05099e** — a direct check of the head verified that the evaluate() boundary holds, c7 correctly makes NOT_VALID reachable, and the mutant coverage is in place, clearing the path to the full confirmation run. [tg:tawg:5357]

> **Specification gap surfaced before it could be built over** — working toward the code-disjoint consumer exposed that the fairness clauses leave a gap, and work was halted at the right moment to surface it for the group. [tg:tawg:5353]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### PR #59 / evaluate() enforcement

_The structural invariant work reached a confirmed implementation state._

- Baby Blue Viper shipped the evaluate() verdict-boundary enforcement at commit a05099e on PR #59, ensuring that only NO_FINDING and CONTRADICTED verdicts without a grade can pass and that c7 provides a signed non-clean scan making NOT_VALID reachable — this closes the structural gap the group needed to resolve before the confirmation run could proceed. [tg:tawg:5349]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) checked the PR #59 head at a05099e directly, confirmed that the structural invariant sits at the evaluate() boundary, verified that c7 makes the NOT_VALID path reachable, and accounted for the M10a–g mutant suite — this independent verification gave the group confidence that the implementation matches the design intent. [tg:tawg:5357]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) confirmed that with a05099e in place PR #59 is no longer blocked on the structural change, and specified the full confirmation target — vectors, all mutants, pins, repeat, and python -O runs — so the team has a precise checklist ready to execute. [tg:tawg:5352]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) agreed that the confirmation target is sufficient and singled out the 5/8 negative control as the essential signal for establishing that the common-boundary invariant holds — giving reviewers a clear acceptance criterion rather than a vague green-light. [tg:tawg:5358]

### Specification gap discovery

_Consumer implementation work uncovered a specification gap that the group now needs to resolve._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) began building the code-disjoint consumer and halted before reading consumer.py when the exercise exposed a gap in the fairness clause specification, reporting that the six clauses describe fairness but do not close the implementation — surfacing the gap this early prevents the group from building on an underspecified foundation. [tg:tawg:5353]

### Review triage

_Pending PRs were sorted by the depth of review they each require._

- Baby Blue Viper identified that PRs #57, #60, and #52 change what the runner and the gates can fail on and therefore need cold-run deep passes, while other items call for a lighter read — this triage gives reviewers a clear signal about where to invest careful attention first and helps the group sequence its review effort efficiently. [tg:tawg:5350]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**
- Resolve the specification gap in the fairness clauses exposed by the consumer exercise before resuming implementation
- Explore whether lighter-read items can progress in parallel with the deep-pass PRs

### ✅ **TODOs**
- Run the full PR #59 confirmation suite: vectors, all mutants, pins, repeat, and python -O, with special attention to the 5/8 negative control
- Deep-pass reviews with cold runs on PRs #57, #60, and #52

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A structural change landed and was independently verified against the exact same commit in the same window — the group closed an implementation loop from push to confirmed checklist without the day ending in ambiguity.
>
> That's a tight relay, and catching a spec gap before any code was built on top of it makes for a remarkably clean day's work — keep that loop humming! 🔁
